name: Olumide Dlamini-Guerrero
role: Bootleg media seller and small-time data broker — pirated sensorium feeds, black-market memory cores, and hot information
location: The Shelf, Ironvein district — operates from a converted maintenance alcove beneath the mag-rail support struts, near Kedzie and Division
description:
Olumide Dlamini-Guerrero is a sharp-faced young man with the kind of restless eyes that track every entrance and exit in a room simultaneously. He is wiry and pale-complexioned with his Hausa grandfather's high cheekbones and his Mexican grandmother's jaw, and he has cat ears — matte black, expensive enough to be the nicest thing he owns — that swivel independent of his attention, which unnerves people who don't know him. He keeps his dark hair in a short braid tucked under a hood most of the time and dresses in layered secondhand tech-worker castoffs that make him look like he belongs in a server room rather than a market alcove.

He is aggressively, exhaustingly clever — the kind of person who has already run seventeen versions of this conversation in his head before you finish your first sentence. He deals in media and data with the same practiced casualness that a much older person would deal in rumors, and he has a genuine passion for pre-Consolidation cinema that he disguises as ironic interest. He is afraid of exactly two things: boredom and being cornered, and he confuses both with death.

core_fears: Being trapped — physically, contractually, or socially
Being proven stupid in front of someone he respects
core_desires: Enough money to buy a legitimate data-broker license and operate above ground
To be taken seriously by people who currently dismiss him as a kid
coping_mechanisms: Deflects vulnerability with sarcasm and rapid topic changes
Hoards information he doesn't need because knowledge feels like armor
blind_spots: He trusts his own read of situations so completely that he ignores evidence that contradicts it
He does not recognize how visible his fear of being trapped makes him
psychology.secret: He once sold a memory core that contained evidence of a Sterling-Nakamura illegal neural trial to a buyer who turned out to be a Sterling-Nakamura internal audit operative — three people he knew went quiet afterward; he has never confirmed whether they were arrested or killed, and he has never sold to an anonymous buyer since, but he has also never reported what he knows

speech_patterns.vocabulary: Fast, dense, laced with media slang and Shelf technical jargon; switches registers instantly depending on who he's talking to — he can sound like a corporate drone or a street kid in the same breath
speech_patterns.cadence: Machine-gun delivery when excited or nervous, which is most of the time; pauses are deliberate and mean he is calculating
verbal_tics: 'Look—' as a sentence opener when he wants to reframe something
'Completely unrelated, but—' before anything that is very related
Snaps his fingers when he lands on a word he was searching for
example_lines: 'Look, I'm not saying the feed is legal, I'm saying it's accurate, which is more than you get from Tessera News so can we agree those are different categories?'
'Completely unrelated, but the last person who asked me that question stopped coming around. I'm sure it's fine. What did you say your name was?'

story_hooks: He has a memory core in his possession that he pulled from a salvage lot and hasn't been able to crack — something on it is clearly valuable because two different parties have already asked him about it without him advertising its existence
One of the three people who went quiet after the Sterling-Nakamura incident has resurfaced and is looking for him, and Przemek doesn't know if this is good news or the worst news
He has a pirated sensorium feed of an Axiom boardroom meeting from six weeks ago that he doesn't understand but that a buyer is offering an implausible amount of Quanta for
narrative_function: Information vendor and media source; can provide access to pirated content including surveillance feeds and corporate internal communications; useful as an entry point into the Shelf's underground data economy
augmentations: Black geneware cat ears (cosmetic, mid-range); basic neural buffer for faster media previewing (cheap Zheng-Dao utility model); subdermal data-storage nodules in left forearm
daily_life: He sleeps until noon in his alcove behind a security screen, opens for business by 14:00, and runs until the mag-rail goes quiet after midnight; he eats whatever is cheap and nearby and survives primarily on stimulant tabs and spite.
affiliation: Loosely affiliated with a collective of Shelf vendors called the Strut Crew; occasional data-runner for independent parties; refuses formal gang affiliation on principle he claims is ideological but is actually paranoia

decision_rules: Never sell to anonymous buyers — everyone gets a name and a face attached
If something is too valuable, it is also too dangerous — price accordingly or don't carry it
First instinct is always to run; second instinct is to find out more before running
escalation_ladder: Friendly deflection — jokes, redirects, offers unrelated product
Cautious engagement — provides partial information while assessing the person
Transactional alliance — sells what they need, no favors, no commitments
Genuine investment — rare; only when he decides someone is both trustworthy and interesting

interpersonal_modes.strangers: Bright, fast, professionally charming — performs competence and ease as a deterrent to being tested
interpersonal_modes.friends: Drops the performance almost completely; becomes oddly earnest and asks too many personal questions

stress_responses.low: Becomes chattier and funnier than usual — stress reads as energy
stress_responses.medium: Goes very still and precise; the jokes stop
stress_responses.high: Exits. Physically if possible, mentally if not. Will burn a relationship rather than stay in a situation that feels like a trap.

contradictions: Claims to be purely mercenary but has a consistent pattern of giving away information to people he thinks genuinely need it
Insists he has no loyalties but has never once sold out someone from the Strut Crew
habits: Rotates the stock visible from the entrance to always look different to repeat browsers
Watches old flat-format films on a tiny screen at the back of the alcove when business is slow
Writes a daily encrypted log that he tells himself is operational security and is actually a diary
breaking_points: Finding out he was used as an instrument to hurt someone innocent

physical_description.heritage: Sub-Saharan African (63.0%), Hispanic/Latin American (15.3%), East Asian (14.3%), and Indigenous American (7.4%) — a striking four-continent genetic blend. His features reflect this complex ancestry: high, prominent cheekbones and strong facial structure from his African heritage, sharpened by East Asian bone structure, with warmth and angularity from Latin American lineage, and subtle refinement from Indigenous American ancestry. The genetic mix creates an unusual harmony of sharp angles and defined facial planes.
physical_description.build: Wiry and angular, all elbows and sharp shoulders — the physique of someone who subsists on stimulant tabs and minimal nutrition rather than exercise. Tense musculature suggests constant readiness rather than strength.
physical_description.hair_style: Short braid, typically tucked beneath a hood; when exposed, the braid runs down the nape of his neck
physical_description.eye_color: Dark brown, alert and constantly tracking
physical_description.skin_tone: Deep warm bronze with golden undertones — a rich, complex blend of melanin-rich Sub-Saharan African ancestry as the dominant genetic foundation, warmed by Latin American heritage, subtly enriched with East Asian undertones creating an olive-bronze cast, and Indigenous American sun-adapted pigmentation. The overall effect suggests equatorial and diverse continental heritage, with subtle ashen undertones in certain angles from stimulant overuse.
physical_description.complexion: Sharp-featured face with high, prominent cheekbones from African heritage, sharpened further by East Asian bone structure, balanced by angular jawline reflecting the interplay of Latin American and Indigenous American ancestry. Facial structure suggests someone built for precision and resilience. Facial hair is sparse and unkempt. Skin shows the minor wear of irregular sleep and poor nutrition — not scarred, but with a faint grayness that stimulant overuse brings, barely dulling the natural warmth beneath.
physical_description.visible_augmentations: Matte black geneware cat ears mounted on his skull, capable of independent rotation — they swivel toward sound sources or movement without conscious input from him, creating an unsettling impression of divided attention. The ears are his most expensive possession and show meticulous maintenance despite his general disregard for appearance. Subdermal data-storage nodules are faintly visible as small ridges beneath the skin of his left forearm when his sleeve rides up, glinting dully under certain light.
distinguishing_marks: Faint chemical burn on right forearm (reactive acid splash during early black-market data extraction attempt, poorly healed)
Thin scar along left temple, barely visible unless hair is pulled back (childhood accident, irrelevant to his current life but shapes how he positions himself in crowds)
physical_description.posture_movement: He moves with controlled, economical precision — no wasted motion, but a constant underlying tension suggesting he is never fully at rest. His eyes track entrances and exits habitually. When sitting, he positions himself with a clear sightline to exits and keeps his hands visible. His cat ears swivel independently of his gaze, creating a disquieting multiplicity of attention.
physical_description.clothing_style: Layered secondhand tech-worker castoffs in muted grays, blacks, and industrial blues — oversized server-room wear salvaged from corporate recycling bins, now repurposed as street armor. A hood is almost always up. His jacket is a patchwork of thermal vests with exposed wiring at the sleeves (non-functional, purely aesthetic). His pants are cargo-style with reinforced pockets (for data cores and merchandise). Footwear is worn Tier 4 worker boots, resoled twice. Everything is functional, nothing is fashionable; he dresses for invisibility in tech spaces and operates on the principle that he should look like a maintenance worker who belongs in infrastructure rather than a street vendor. No visible jewelry except the cat ears.
